title: The Garden Remembers the Machine
proposition: A mostly white garden where botanical life and used machinery remember one another through touch, weather, repair, tea, and time—fragile but never decorative, mechanical but never sterile.
subjects: cherry roots threading through a dismantled radio
white camellias growing from an open relay cabinet
tea steam passing through a punched brass screen
a cracked porcelain cup beside a rain-darkened motor
plum petals caught inside a watchmaker's gears
moss covering the keys of an abandoned switchboard
a paper lantern wired to a flowering circuit board
seed pods arranged beside worn turbine blades
a greenhouse window repaired with copper traces
fallen blossoms collecting around a silent tram bell
fern shadows crossing a ceramic control panel
a mechanical bird drinking from a stone tea basin
details: one repaired joint held by red thread
a single petal resting on an oil stain
tiny beside a pale mechanism too large to fit
only the shadow joining the living and machined forms
rain beads tracing one interrupted electrical path
a hand-written maintenance mark almost washed away
one moving part while the garden remains still
a hairline crack continuing into a drawn circuit

surfaces.medium_clause: wet grey ink blooms into warm white paper, one black mechanical line
carved grey and tea-brown planes leave most of the paper untouched
fine bitten lines and pale plate tone dissolve into generous white margins
thin chalk-white layers hold minute botanical and copper marks
pale stone ink and one misregistered vermilion plate cross unprinted paper

moods: high white daylight, shadows barely present, one warm metallic glint
quiet overcast light, pearl grey and bone, one tea-brown trace
morning haze through glass, pale mint at the furthest edge
white ground after rain, one reflected signal-red mark
soft window light, chalk and porcelain, the darkest value very small
